claim: The TetO-MYC/TetO-Neu/MMTV-rtTA transgenic mouse model recapitulates hallmarks of human breast disease.
source: For modeling tumorigenesis in breast tissue, we use an inducible mouse model of breast cancer (TetO-MYC/TetO-Neu/MMTV-rtTA transgenic mice) (Fry et al., 2016; Moody et al., 2002; Podsypanina et al., 2008) that has been shown to recapitulate hallmarks of human breast disease (Havas et al., 2017; Jechlinger et al., 2009; Figure 1a).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies (Havas et al., 2017; Jechlinger et al., 2009) that demonstrated this property of the mouse model.

claim: The activity of MYC and Neu oncogenes is under the control of a Tet-O promoter that can only be activated in the presence of both rtTA protein and doxycycline compound.
source: In this tractable transgenic mouse model, the activity of two potent oncogenes – MYC and Neu (the rodent homolog for the human ERBB2 gene used in this mouse model)– are under the control of a Tet-O promoter that can only be activated in the presence of both the rtTA (reverse tetracycline-controlled transactivator) protein and the doxycycline compound.
evidence: This is a description of the genetic system design, which is established knowledge about Tet-inducible systems.

claim: The MMTV promoter confines expression of the rtTA protein to cells of the mammary lineage.
source: This three-part inducible system allows for temporal control of oncogenic expression by regulating doxycycline in the medium or animal diet and spatial control by the MMTV promoter that confines expression of the rtTA protein to the cells of the mammary lineage (Bockamp et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bockamp et al., 2002, which established this property of the MMTV promoter.

claim: The bi-transgenic model allows acini to present with two cell populations – tumorigenic and non-tumorigenic.
source: Hence, this novel (B) model should allow acini to present with two cell populations –tumorigenic and non-tumorigenic– and could be used to study the dynamics of early tumorigenesis in an otherwise normal epithelium (Figure 1a, lower right panels).
evidence: This is a logical inference from the experimental design where only lentivirally transduced cells express rtTA and can activate oncogenes.

claim: MYC oncogene protein is expressed in only the transduced cells of bi-transgenic acini as opposed to all cells of tri-transgenic acini.
source: Immunofluorescent staining of 3D matrigel cultures, for both sets of doxycycline-induced transduced acini, was used to validate transgene specific protein expression of the MYC oncogene (human) in only the transduced cells of (B) acini as opposed to all cells of (T) acini (Figure 1b, anti-human MYC specific antibody).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1b demonstrating differential MYC expression patterns.

claim: 800 ng/ml doxycycline in the tissue wide system and 600 ng/ml doxycycline in the stochastic system produce the same mRNA expression levels of oncogenes.
source: This way we normalized doxycycline dosage in both systems to obtain the same mRNA expression levels of oncogenes using 800 ng/ml doxycycline in the tissue wide (T) system and 600 ng/ml doxycycline in the stochastic (B) system (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 comparing mRNA expression levels at different doxycycline concentrations.

claim: Lentivirus-transduced structures from the tissue wide induction system presented with filled lumens containing both infected and non-infected oncogene-expressing cells.
source: Lentivirus-transduced structures from the tissue wide induction system (T) presented with filled lumens that contained both infected (GFP positive) as well as non-infected oncogene-expressing cells.
evidence: This is an observation from immunofluorescent staining experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: Tissue wide induction system structures exhibited overall disrupted epithelial polarity and some random microlumen.
source: These structures exhibited overall disrupted epithelial polarity and some random microlumen, as reported previously (Jechlinger et al., 2009; Figure 2a).
evidence: Supported by both current observations (Figure 2a) and previous report (Jechlinger et al., 2009).

claim: Some bi-transgenic acini showed exclusively H2B-GFP marked cells in hyperplastic areas that displayed double cell rim morphology and disturbed epithelial polarity after 96 hr of oncogene expression.
source: For the stochastic tumor induction system (B), we observed 2 phenotypes after 96 hr of oncogene expression; some of the (B) acini showed exclusively H2B-GFP marked cells in hyperplastic areas that also displayed double cell rim morphology and disturbed epithelial polarity (Figures 2a and 96 hours ON DOX, left panels)
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 2a at 96 hours post-induction.

claim: Some bi-transgenic acini did not show expansion of the few H2B-GFP positive cells after 96 hr of oncogene expression.
source: while the other (B) acini did not show expansion of the few H2B-GFP positive cells (Figures 2a and 96 hours ON DOX, right panels).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 2a at 96 hours post-induction.

claim: Multi layered regions in acini contained mainly H2B-GFP positive cells that stained for MYC.
source: We verified that multi layered regions in acini contained mainly H2B-GFP positive cells that expectedly stained for MYC (Figure 2b, middle panels).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 2b middle panels.

claim: The inability of single H2B-GFP positive, transduced cells to expand over 96 hr was not due to the lack of MYC expression.
source: For normal appearing regions, this analysis showed that the inability of single H2B-GFP positive, transduced cells to expand over 96 hr was not due to the lack of MYC expression (Figure 2b, lower panels).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2b lower panels showing MYC expression in non-expanding cells.

claim: The InVI SPIM was adjusted for non-phototoxic, long-term imaging up to 4 days, every 10 min with 1 µm z-spacing.
source: The InVI SPIM was adjusted for non-phototoxic, long-term imaging (up to 4 days, every 10 min with 1 µm z-spacing).
evidence: This describes the imaging parameters established for the experiments.

claim: Tri-transgenic acini transduced with reporter virus proliferated swiftly upon doxycycline addition showing expansion of both marked and unmarked cells.
source: The T/H2B-mCherry acini transduced with reporter virus proliferated swiftly upon doxycycline addition showing expansion of both the marked and unmarked cells (Figure 3a)
evidence: Supported by light-sheet microscopy imaging data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: A sturdy tumor phenotype developed in tri-transgenic acini, manifested by multi-cell-layered rims and pronounced proliferation-associated-apoptosis in all acini.
source: a sturdy tumor phenotype developed, manifested by multi-cell-layered rims and pronounced proliferation-associated-apoptosis in all acini (Figure 3—Video 1).
evidence: Supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 3—Video 1.

claim: Some bi-transgenic acini showed fast clonal expansion of oncogene-expressing cells that form multilayer clusters in the acinus rim.
source: Some acini showed fast clonal expansion of oncogene-expressing cells that form multilayer clusters in the acinus rim.
evidence: This is an observation from light-sheet microscopy time-lapse imaging of bi-transgenic acini.

claim: The proliferative phenotype in bi-transgenic acini stems from several transduced cells in vicinity to each other at the start of time-lapse imaging.
source: This proliferative phenotype seems to stem from several transduced cells in vicinity to each other at the start of time-lapse imaging (Figure 3b, upper panel; Figure 3—Video 2).
evidence: Supported by light-sheet microscopy imaging data shown in Figure 3b upper panel and Figure 3—Video 2.

claim: More sparsely infected bi-transgenic acini did not sustain proliferation of the oncogene-expressing cells.
source: Again, more sparsely infected acini, did not sustain proliferation of the oncogene-expressing cells (Figure 3b, lower panel; Figure 3—Video 3).
evidence: Supported by light-sheet microscopy imaging data shown in Figure 3b lower panel and Figure 3—Video 3.

claim: The phenotypes for bi-transgenic and tri-transgenic acini are consistent with the respective behavior observed with the 96 hr end point immunofluorescent analysis.
source: Taken together, the phenotypes for (B) and (T) acini are consistent with the respective behavior observed with the 96 hr end point immunofluorescent analysis (Figure 2a and b), verifying these prior observations and excluding phototoxic effects due to longitudinal SPIM imaging.
evidence: This is a comparison between two different experimental approaches (immunofluorescence and live imaging) showing consistent results.

claim: The average True Positive to Ground Truth ratio for segmentation accuracy is 0.92.
source: The average True Positive to Ground Truth ratio for the four timepoints is 0.92.
evidence: Supported by segmentation accuracy assessment data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Single transduced cells within one acinus show a difference in proliferation and cell fate.
source: Cell tracking allowed us to follow the clonal evolution for each transduced cell in the acinus over 3 days. Single transduced cells within one acinus show a difference in proliferation and cell fate as indicated in representative tracks (Figure 4a).
evidence: Supported by single-cell tracking data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: The number of transduced cells in the cluster is the most important feature that can predict whether a cluster can form a tumor.
source: In this model only one feature, the 'number of transduced cells in the cluster', can predict whether a cluster can form a tumor.
evidence: Supported by logistic regression model selection analysis based on Akaike information criterion.

claim: Each additional transduced cell in a cluster increases the odds of this cluster forming a tumor by 9.
source: Each additional transduced cell in a cluster increases the odds of this cluster forming a tumor by 9 (Figure 4b, lower right panel).
evidence: Supported by logistic regression analysis results shown in Figure 4b lower right panel.

claim: Acini with tumors only differed significantly from those without tumor on the number and proliferation rate of transduced cells.
source: Acini with tumors only differed significantly from those without tumor on the number and proliferation rate of transduced cells in line with the observation that clusters of transduced cells are the primary indicators of tumor outcome.
evidence: Supported by comparison of acinus-level features shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1a.

claim: In the mixed model regression analysis, the number of oncogene-expressing cells in the cluster appeared as the main contributing factor to tumorigenesis with an odds ratio of 6.7.
source: In this model again, the number of oncogene-expressing cells in the cluster appeared as the main contributing factor to tumorigenesis with an odds ratio of 6.7 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: Supported by mixed model regression analysis results shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Tumors are mainly initiated by clusters of transduced cells.
source: That tumors are mainly initiated by clusters of transduced cells is further illustrated by representative acini shown in Figure 4c
evidence: Supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4c demonstrating cluster-based tumor initiation.

claim: Proliferating cells that establish tumor foci at the end of the long-term imaging cluster together at the start of the time lapse imaging.
source: proliferating cells that establish tumor foci at the end of the long-term imaging cluster together at the start of the time lapse imaging and the non-proliferative cells are more sparsely located within the acinus.
evidence: Supported by time-lapse imaging analysis comparing initial and final cell positions.

claim: Similar sized acini bearing the same number of transduced cells showed differential cluster expansion depending on the numbers of transduced cells within a cluster.
source: In line, we found examples of similar sized acini bearing the same number of transduced cells that showed differential cluster expansion depending on the 'numbers of transduced cells within a cluster' (Figure 4—figure supplement 2; comparison a to b).
evidence: Supported by comparative imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Clusters of single cells do not expand over time, whereas clusters containing several cells show massive expansion.
source: Consequently, and again depending on the number of cells within the specific cluster, we observed clusters behaving differently within the same organoid; the organoids shown in Figure 4a, Figure 4c (top and middle panels) and Figure 4—figure supplement 2a, display clusters of single cells that do not expand over time, whereas clusters containing several cells show massive expansion (beyond normal expected cells division rates due to growth of the acinus).
evidence: Supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in multiple figures (4a, 4c, and Figure 4—figure supplement 2a).

claim: A proximity-controlled interaction or signaling network between different transformed cells might guide tumor outgrowth in a normal epithelium.
source: Our results indicate that a proximity-controlled interaction or signaling network between different transformed cells might guide tumor outgrowth in a normal epithelium (Greaves and Maley, 2012; Reid et al., 2010).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results, supported by citations to related concepts in the literature.

claim: An intact polarized tissue layer exerts a repressive effect on single early stage cancerous cells.
source: This might be due to the repressive effect that an intact polarized tissue layer exerts on single early stage cancerous cells (Lee and Vasioukhin, 2008).
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by citation to Lee and Vasioukhin, 2008.

claim: The simple parameter of 'number of transduced cells within a cluster' is enough to impinge on overall epithelial integrity.
source: According to our modeling attempts the simple parameter of 'number of transduced cells within a cluster' is enough to impinge on overall epithelial integrity and most likely already accounts for sub-features like 'distances between transduced cells in a cluster volume' or 'number of cell-cell contacts between transduced cells in a cluster volume', which did not pan out as predictive factors on their own.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the statistical modeling results presented earlier in the manuscript.

claim: The increased probability for tumor outgrowth upon proximity effects of closely located transformed cells might be rooted in paracrine effects.
source: In addition, the increased probability for tumor outgrowth upon proximity effects of closely located transformed cells, might also be rooted in paracrine effects (e.g. via microRNAs [Kosaka et al., 2012] in the cluster, or hydrogen ion dynamics/pH [Reshkin et al., 2014]).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the results, supported by citations to relevant mechanisms in the literature.

claim: Loss of important polarity proteins has been highlighted as functioning as non-canonical tumor suppressors in breast tumorigenesis.
source: Studies on loss of important polarity proteins have highlighted their function as non-canonical tumor suppressors in breast tumorigenesis (McCaffrey et al., 2012; Partanen et al., 2012)
evidence: Supported by citations to McCaffrey et al., 2012 and Partanen et al., 2012.

claim: Other reports cannot confirm the observations about polarity proteins as tumor suppressors, which were all obtained from tissue wide transformed model systems.
source: however, other reports (Macara and McCaffrey, 2013; Xue et al., 2013) cannot confirm these observations which were all obtained from tissue wide transformed model systems, leaving conclusions open for alternative studies.
evidence: Supported by citations to conflicting reports (Macara and McCaffrey, 2013; Xue et al., 2013).

claim: Cells within a polarized, differentiated epithelial cell layer are able to establish tumorigenic outgrowth upon stochastic activation of strong oncogenic drivers.
source: We report that cells within a polarized, differentiated epithelial cell layer are able to establish tumorigenic outgrowth upon stochastic activation of strong oncogenic drivers, supporting the concept of interconversion between differentiated- and stem-like states (Chaffer and Weinberg, 2015; Gupta et al., 2011; Plaks et al., 2015) for tumor initiating cells.
evidence: Supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript and related to concepts in cited literature.

claim: Not all cells expressing the combination of MYC and Neu oncogenes can expand, demonstrating an inhibitory effect that needs to stem from the normal epithelial microenvironment.
source: However, not all cells expressing the very powerful combination of MYC and Neu oncogenes can expand, demonstrating an inhibitory effect that needs to stem from the normal epithelial microenvironment in the presented system.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental observations showing differential expansion of oncogene-expressing cells.

claim: ERBB2 is overexpressed in approximately 20% of breast cancers.
source: ERBB2 is overexpressed in ~20% of breast cancers (Arteaga et al., 2012)
evidence: Supported by citation to Arteaga et al., 2012.

claim: MYC is overexpressed in 15-50% of human breast cancer.
source: MYC in 15–50% of human breast cancer (Blancato et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to Blancato et al., 2004.

claim: The combination of MYC and ERBB2 is found in highly aggressive human breast cancer.
source: The combination of MYC and ERBB2 is found in highly aggressive human breast cancer (Al-Kuraya et al., 2004)
evidence: Supported by citation to Al-Kuraya et al., 2004.

claim: Neu and MYC strongly accelerate tumor onset in combined transgenic animals (average 45 days) as compared to single transgenic animals (MYC 155 days, Neu 99 days).
source: and - in fact- Neu (the rodent homolog for the human ERBB2 gene used in this mouse model) and MYC strongly accelerate tumor onset In the combined transgenic animals (average 45 days) as compared to single transgenic animals (MYC 155 days, Neu 99 days)
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mouse model being used, likely from previous characterization studies.

claim: Tumors regress rapidly to non-palpable state following oncogene silencing in the transgenic mouse model.
source: In all cases tumors regress rapidly to non-palpable state following oncogene silencing.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the reversibility of the transgenic mouse model being used.

claim: Primary mammary epithelial cells were seeded in 3D matrigel as single cells and grown for 48 hr to form small acini consisting of around 15 cells that arrange around a small lumen.
source: Primary mammary epithelial cells derived from transgenic mice were seeded in 3D matrigel as single cells to be grown for 48 hr to form small acini consisting of around 15 cells that arrange around a small lumen.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol used in the study.

claim: The c-MYC antibody (Cell Signaling Technologies, Cat. # D84C12) recognizes specifically the human protein and does not recognize endogenous mouse MYC protein.
source: Please note that the c-MYC antibody (Cell Signaling Technologies, Cat. # D84C12) recognizes specifically the human protein, which is transgenically expressed and does not recognize endogenous mouse MYC protein.
evidence: This is technical information about the antibody specificity used in the experiments.

claim: Long-term imaging of primary organoids has been achieved via light-sheet microscopy.
source: Long-term imaging of primary organoids has been achieved via light-sheet microscopy (Drost et al., 2015; Serra et al., 2019; Verissimo et al., 2016)
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies (Drost et al., 2015; Serra et al., 2019; Verissimo et al., 2016).

claim: Light-sheet microscopy efforts have benefited from the lower phototoxicity provided by SPIM imaging.
source: and these efforts have benefited from the lower phototoxicity provided by SPIM imaging.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the advantages of SPIM imaging technology.

claim: Tracking single-cell dynamics in fast dividing tumor organoid cells necessitates high resolution imaging which limits the time frame in which organoids can be imaged without phototoxic effects.
source: However, regarding fast dividing cells in tumor organoids, tracking single-cell dynamics necessitates high resolution imaging which in turn limits the time frame in which organoids can be imaged without phototoxic effects (Held et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Held et al., 2018.

claim: Imaging primary organoids for longer time periods requires an offset of temporal and cellular resolution that eventually cannot allow single-cell fate tracking.
source: Conversely, imaging primary organoids for longer time periods requires an offset of temporal and cellular resolution that eventually cannot allow single-cell fate tracking (Dekkers et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Dekkers et al., 2016.

claim: The hierarchical model refers to tumor propagating cells as cancer stem cells (CSCs).
source: Two models have been used to understand tumor progression and heterogeneity (Plaks et al., 2015); the (i) hierarchical model refers to tumor propagating cells as cancer stem cells (CSCs) (Kreso and Dick, 2014)
evidence: Supported by citations to Plaks et al., 2015 and Kreso and Dick, 2014.

claim: The stochastic model states that every cell within a tumor is equally likely to be the cell of origin and facilitate tumor initiation and progression.
source: and the (ii) stochastic model states that every cell within a tumor is equally likely to be the cell of origin and facilitate tumor initiation and progression (Vogelstein et al., 1988; Williams et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to Vogelstein et al., 1988 and Williams et al., 2007.

claim: Models for tumor propagation can be reconciled when considering that the population of oncogene driven cells have the capacity to interconvert between differentiated- and stem-like states.
source: These models for tumor propagation can be reconciled when considering that the population of oncogene driven cells have the capacity to interconvert between differentiated- and stem-like states (Chaffer and Weinberg, 2015; Gupta et al., 2011; Plaks et al., 2015)
evidence: Supported by citations to Chaffer and Weinberg, 2015; Gupta et al., 2011; and Plaks et al., 2015.

claim: The flexibility of cells to interconvert between differentiated- and stem-like states is supported by the microenvironment.
source: a flexibility that is supported by the microenvironment (McGovern et al., 2009; Quail et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to McGovern et al., 2009 and Quail et al., 2012.

claim: The concepts of hierarchical and stochastic models have not been probed in the context of tumor initiation upon stochastic oncogene activation in an established cell-layer.
source: These concepts, however, have not been probed in the context of tumor initiation upon stochastic oncogene activation in an established cell-layer.
evidence: This identifies a gap in the literature that the current study addresses.

claim: The study presents a novel model of breast tumorigenesis where only single cells express oncogenes within healthy mammary acini and are able to establish localized outgrowth.
source: Here we present a novel model of breast tumorigenesis where only single cells express oncogenes within healthy mammary acini and are able to establish localized outgrowth.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main contribution of the manuscript.

claim: The study overcomes limitations of studying tumorigenesis events in the face of tissue-wide transformation.
source: We thereby overcome the above-mentioned limitations of studying tumorigenesis events in the face of tissue-wide transformation.
evidence: This is a claim about the advantage of the new model system developed in the study.

claim: The study performs long-term imaging of stochastic breast tumor acini for the first time at a temporal resolution that allows following single-cell fates.
source: Furthermore, we perform long-term imaging of these stochastic breast tumor acini for the first time at a temporal resolution that allows us to follow single-cell fates.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the imaging approach used in the study.

claim: The study integrates the imaging approach with an image analysis pipeline capable of segmenting cells in their dynamic progression towards tumorigenesis and tracking them individually over time.
source: We also integrate this approach with an image analysis pipeline capable of segmenting cells in their dynamic progression towards tumorigenesis, so they can be tracked individually over time.
evidence: This describes the computational analysis component developed for the study.

claim: Small local clusters of transformed cells form tumors while isolated transformed cells do not.
source: The power of this integrated approach is illustrated by us finding that small local clusters of transformed cells form tumors while isolated transformed cells do not.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by the experimental data and analysis presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Organoid cultures grown from cell-lines or primary cells have been successfully employed to study molecular mechanisms during different stages of tumorigenesis.
source: Organoid cultures grown from cell-lines or primary cells have been successfully employed to study molecular mechanisms during different stages of tumorigenesis (Clevers, 2016; Havas et al., 2017; Simian and Bissell, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Clevers, 2016; Havas et al., 2017; and Simian and Bissell, 2017.

claim: Organoids are derived from primary material that usually allows oncogenic activation in all cells of the tissue and therefore cannot reproduce the localized expansion at a defined part of the tissue that is seen in the patient situation.
source: However, they are derived from primary material that usually allows oncogenic activation in all cells of the tissue and therefore cannot reproduce the localized expansion at a defined part of the tissue that is seen in the patient situation.
evidence: This identifies a limitation of existing organoid models.

claim: To study tumor initiation, models need to be established wherein only a few tumorigenic cells expand in the context of its immediate non-tumor microenvironment.
source: To study tumor initiation, models need to be established wherein only a few tumorigenic cells expand in the context of its immediate non-tumor microenvironment (Tabassum and Polyak, 2015) and the interplay of these populations can be visualized.
evidence: This is a statement about what is needed in the field, supported by citation to Tabassum and Polyak, 2015.

claim: The ability to distinguish marked tumor cells from the normal epithelium will allow performing single-cell RNA sequencing analysis on select sorted cells.
source: The ability to distinguish marked tumor cells from the normal epithelium will now allow us to perform single-cell RNA sequencing analysis on select sorted cells.
evidence: This is a statement about future applications enabled by the model system.

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing will help delineate the signaling networks within the immediate tumor microenvironment and further clarify the molecular basis of these distinct processes.
source: This will help delineate the signaling networks within the immediate tumor microenvironment and further clarify the molecular basis of these distinct processes.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about what future experiments might reveal.

claim: The amenability of 3D multicellular systems to interference with small molecule inhibitors, viral shRNA vectors and genomic editing has the potential to further understanding of mechanisms important during tumor initiation.
source: The amenability of 3D multicellular systems to interference with small molecule inhibitors, viral shRNA vectors and genomic editing has the potential to further our understanding of the mechanisms important during tumor initiation.
evidence: This is a statement about potential future applications of the system.

claim: The system will permit drug screens on the heterogeneous populations of normal and malignant cells.
source: In the future, this will also permit drug screens on the heterogeneous populations of normal and malignant cells, as presented in the described stochastic breast tumor model.
evidence: This is a statement about potential future applications of the model system.

claim: The ability to follow tumor regression and establishment of minimal residual disease within a tissue like acinus structure will help distinguish between overall cytotoxic drugs and tumor cell specific inhibitory drugs.
source: The ability to follow tumor regression and establishment of minimal residual disease within a tissue like acinus structure will help distinguish between overall cytotoxic drugs and tumor cell specific inhibitory drugs.
evidence: This is a statement about potential future applications of the system for drug testing.

claim: The integration of a true stochastic tumor model with the ability to image single-cell fates will successfully bridge the gap between genetically modified model systems and the clinical situation.
source: Taken together, we strongly believe that our integration of a true stochastic tumor model with the ability to image single-cell fates will successfully bridge the gap between genetically modified model systems and the clinical situation, helping gain novel insights on breast cancer.
evidence: This is a concluding statement about the significance and potential impact of the work.
